derived.term: Council district to community board crosswalk
derived.detail: Areal overlap between the shoreline-clipped council district boundaries (872g-cjhh) and the community district boundaries (5crt-au7u), regenerated when either boundary file changes. Percentages are rounded to a whole number and approximate; on a board the denominator is that board, on a district it is that district. The boards dataset also carries a council_district column, which holds 44 distinct values across 59 rows and omits 7 council districts — it records the board office's district rather than the districts a board covers, so it is not used for this join.
Hearing start plus 72 hours. Adjournment times are not published and adjournment is at or after the start, so the stamp is a provable lower bound on the real deadline rather than the deadline.
Three business days before the hearing, against a committed holiday table.

cited.detail: A few dozen land-use hearing notices a year across all 59 community boards. It is the only City dataset carrying dated board notices, and no City dataset publishes a dated board calendar.

Agendas, minutes and the meeting location are published there and nowhere in the City's data. A board on its own domain rather than a City one is given as text rather than a link, because the host cannot be verified at build time.

caveats: The City publishes no community board meeting calendar, so each of the 59 boards is read from whatever it publishes itself — a feed, a page, a PDF, a scan. A source can answer and still be months behind, which is why the Community boards program reports both.
Community board meeting cadence is quoted exactly as ruf7-3wgc records it. That is the City's record of the cadence, and it has been observed to disagree with what boards publish on their own sites.
ruf7-3wgc records the board office address, not the meeting venue. Committees often sit at the office and the full board often does not.
Unlike Council committees, which are called by their chair, a community board meets on a standing monthly cadence.

Budget requests are an annual filing rather than current activity: the register appears a few times a year, so an entry can be months old. A board shows the newest edition of the register (vn4m-mk4t) published on or before the build date, capped at five requests with the total stated beside it. Priority numbers repeat because each one ranks within a budget category — capital, capital support, expense.

Agency replies are quoted rather than sorted into yes and no: the phrasing changes between editions of the same row, and it records a position rather than an outcome. A request is not a commitment and not a funded outcome.
The Council Members listed against a board can introduce legislation for that area, and nominate half of the board's members.
Council district geometry ships simplified — 132 KB gzipped against 3.8 MB raw, measured to assign the same district as full precision on 99.99% of a citywide lattice.
No figure anywhere on this site compares one board or district with another.
